Hi Elaine — thanks for the usage file, that was really helpful. I've sketched two realistic constructs below (numbers illustrative):

Option A — Marginal ladder (more upside to you if you concentrate volume):
- 0–100M tokens: $0.00030/token
- 100M–500M: $0.00020/token (marginal price for tokens in the band)
- 500M+: $0.00012/token

If in month 3 you miss the 100M breakpoint, we true-up on actuals at quarter end: tokens are billed at the marginal price for the band they fall into; no retrospective blending. This keeps per-token economics tight and ties discounts to realized velocity.

Option B — Smoothed blended ramp (predictable forecasting):
- You commit to a quarterly nominal band (e.g., 300M tokens/quarter). We compute an effective blended rate monthly for invoicing: total tokens for the quarter * blended rate across bands. If you miss the quarterly commitment by >12%, we apply a smoothing credit in the next quarter (limited to one quarter) rather than clawbacks.

Tradeoffs: Marginal gives you the best possible marginal cost if you exceed bands; blended gives you predictability for forecasting.

I attached a short draft SLA + a pricing workbook with worked examples. Happy to run the DataWave file through our model if you want exact numbers.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine — attached are the two scenario simulations using your actual six months: marginal ladder vs blended quarterly smoothing. Key callouts: 

- Under marginal ladder, DataWave would have saved ~18% last quarter if spikes continued; downside is a potential 7% higher spend in months where volume falls below breakpoints.
- Under blended quarterly invoicing with a smoothing credit, variability reduces to ±2–3% vs plan which helps finance forecasting.

Proposal (commercial):
- Pilot 6 months on blended quarterly invoicing with a 6-month review.
- If DataWave achieves sustained >500M annualized velocity by month 4 of pilot, applied marginal kicker for tokens above 500M for the remaining pilot period (retroactive to the quarter start).
- Single-quarter smoothing credit (up to 10% of the missed commitment) rather than cash clawbacks.

Next steps: procurement to confirm if pilot approach and smoothing guardrail are acceptable; if so, we’ll issue a pilot SOW and finalize the SLA.

Thanks — attaching the worked workbook as promised.

Marcus

Rajiv — great questions. Short answers and a final commercial tweak: 

1) Cap on smoothing credit: yes. We can cap at $75k per quarter for the pilot (fixed-dollar cap) — this keeps CFOs comfortable while preserving smoothing mechanics.
2) Marginal kicker retroactivity: we can apply the marginal kicker retroactively to the start of the quarter in which the velocity threshold was crossed, capped to the quarter (i.e., tokens above 500M that month would be rebilled at the marginal kicker rate and show as an invoice credit for that quarter). That gives you upside if you spike mid-quarter.

Final commercial tweak (to make this low-friction):
- 6-month blended quarterly pilot
- $75k smoothing credit cap per quarter
- Marginal kicker applies retroactively within the quarter once 500M annualized velocity is observed
- One mid-pilot review (month 3) where we can adjust breakpoints if your traffic trends materially change

If that sounds acceptable I’ll have Legal/Finance draft a short pilot SOW and send the DocuSign link.

Cheers,
